construct: Miller Fisher syndrome is an acute immune-mediated Guillain-Barre-spectrum neuropathy classically characterized by ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, and areflexia and is strongly associated with IgG antibodies against the GQ1b ganglioside.

adversarial_second_pass.independent_reconstruction: Postinfectious ophthalmoplegia, ataxia, and areflexia with preserved limb strength is the classic Miller Fisher phenotype, which is strongly associated with IgG anti-GQ1b antibodies.
adversarial_second_pass.strongest_distractor_attack: Anti-GM1 is more associated with axonal Guillain-Barre variants; P/Q-channel antibodies cause Lambert-Eaton; AChR antibodies cause myasthenia gravis; AQP4 antibodies cause NMOSD.
adversarial_second_pass.expert_reviewer_reversal: The preserved limb strength and full Miller Fisher triad prevent ordinary ascending GBS or neuromuscular-junction disorders from becoming equivalent alternatives.
